feasible.reason: The proposal's headline mechanism does not exist in this firmware and cannot exist under the no-battery constraint, and the residual it leaves is bypassed by the realistic evil-maid timeline. (1) "A trip erases BKP0R..7R (BHK) in hardware" destroys nothing: `secure/src/hw/bhk.rs` persists the BHK DHUK-wrapped in flash page 126 and re-installs it into BKP0R..7R on every boot ("we regenerate from flash on every boot anyway", :28-33; `load_and_lock` :286-425). That is forced by the supercap-only VBAT: a key that lived only in the backup domain would vanish every time the device sat unplugged >12-24 h (`docs/security/brownout-hardening.md` :253-256), i.e. in the normal resting state of a slow-money signer. So the tamper response is necessarily software: a TAMP_SR flag read at the next powered boot -> `tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe` (tamp.rs :80-121), which the attacker can pre-empt by simply waiting. (2) Bypass: a cold-storage wallet is unplugged for days, so the attacker almost always arrives at a drained, unarmed device (and in transit, always: the device ships unpowered at RDP-0 and arms only after the first field boot). Cut the mesh, bridge TAMP_OUTy to TAMP_INx at the QFN (the PRNG signal passes through the jumper, so the active comparator is satisfied forever) or re-close the mesh, implant, done; nothing is latched because the backup domain was dead and nothing is detected at re-arm because OUT==IN. The proposal's own risk line ("after that only persistent opens are caught") concedes this; an attacker never leaves it open. What survives is "catch an attacker who acts within ~12-24 h of the last unplug and does not repair two nets" - cost-raising only, not P1 for a board spin. (3) Pin plan is wrong: on the STM32U585 the TAMP_OUT functions are NOT on PA10/PB4 (DS13086 Rev 10 pin table): the 48-pin part's tamper-capable pins are exactly PC13 = TAMP_IN1/TAMP_OUT2, PA0 = TAMP_IN2/TAMP_OUT1, PA1 = TAMP_IN5/TAMP_OUT4 (PB2 has no TAMP function). Active mode needs IN and OUT on two of these, so a button (PA0 LEFT or PA1 RIGHT, pq1.rs :215-218) must move to PA10/PB4 - a bigger board change than "a pin or two". (4) Firmware details: `poll()` only looks at `ITAMP_FLAG_MASK` (tamp.rs :87, :211-221), so external TAMP1F would currently be ignored even if armed; "read ATOR twice per RM0456" is not an RM0456 requirement (RM0456 §64 init procedure: write ATCR, CR1, 4x ATSEEDR, wait SEEDF=0); STM32U575/585 rev X lack the active-tamper prescaler extension; ITAMP5 must be enabled when ATCKSEL[3]=1.
feasible.corrections: If pursued anyway, re-scope and re-rate: priority P2/P3 (post-FSBL/WRP/S-1..S-3), kind=hardware (board spin, button relocation, mesh layers, LSE present or not is irrelevant since LSI is also VBAT-powered on U5 per RM0456 §10 but confirm supercap is actually populated on V10 - hardware_requirements.md :245 still says "board not started"). Mechanism correction: state the response honestly as "TAMPxF latched in the backup domain -> software SE admin-wipe at next boot, valid only while VBAT holds (~12-24 h)"; drop the "hardware erase of BHK" claim, or make BHK backup-only (then every supercap drain bricks the device - not acceptable). Pin correction: TAMP_IN1 on PC13 + TAMP_OUT1 on PA0 (ATOSHARE=0 default pairing) with LEFT KEY moved to PA10, or TAMP_IN5 (PA1) + TAMP_OUT2 (PC13) via ATOSHARE/ATOSEL with RIGHT KEY moved. Firmware: add TAMP1F/TAMP5F to the poll mask and to the boot-time pre-BHK-load check so a latched external trip wipes before `bhk::load_and_lock` re-installs the key; seed from the 3-source TRNG, wait SEEDF=0, re-seed periodically; enable ITAMP5. Honest coverage statement: catches opens/shorts while powered or within the supercap window; gives zero transit coverage and is defeated by waiting for drain + OUT->IN bridge. The vendor precedents that make this class work (GridPlus 5-year battery, potting) are exactly what the owner decision excludes; without a battery, the physical-open class is better served by IMP-01-style destructive/visible shell and the FSBL fingerprint than by an active mesh.

vendor-claim.reason: The vendor_precedent and novelty='parity' fields survive verification. Trezor T3W1 ships ONLY a passive, level-mode TAMP_IN2 armed under PRODUCTION (confirmed in code: no ATCR/ATOR/ATSEEDR anywhere in trezor-firmware; TAMPER_INPUT_2 is defined only for T3W1 revA/B/C). GridPlus Lattice1 demonstrably ships an active LDS mesh with a constant waveform, ~5-year battery, erase+permanent-brick on trip (official docs), so the proposal is parity, not 'beyond'. Foundation Passport Prime officially documents active tamper detection that erases the Master Key on opening/modification, with display-covering tamper pins per its audit response. Keystone's 'PCI-level anti-tamper' is vendor marketing (README) with no published mesh/cert evidence. The cited ST community thread exists at the cited URL (an ST moderator confirms open AND short detection; RM0456 §64.1 says the same) and PC13=TAMP_IN1 is confirmed by RM0456 and DS13086. The claim is therefore not refuted, but it contains a material implementation error (PA10/PB4 carry no TAMP_OUT function on the U585) and several precision issues listed in corrections.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) PIN ERROR (material, not precedent): DS13086 Rev 10 pin table shows PA10 and PB4 have NO TAMP_OUT additional function. On the UFQFPN48 part the only TAMP_OUT pins are TAMP_OUT1=PA0 (pq1 LEFT KEY), TAMP_OUT2=PC13 (same pad as TAMP_IN1, so unusable as its pair), TAMP_OUT4=PA1 (pq1 RIGHT KEY). TAMP_IN2=PA0, TAMP_IN5=PA1; TAMP_IN3/4/6/7/8 live on PE2/PE4/PE5/PE6/PC5 which are not bonded. An active pair on pq1 therefore requires re-routing a button off PA0 or PA1 (then ATOSHARE=1, ATOSEL1=0b11 pairs TAMP_IN1/PC13 with TAMP_OUT4/PA1), or falling back to a Trezor-style passive level-mode mesh on PC13 that cannot detect shorts. Replace 'TAMP_OUT on a second free pad (PA10/PB4 candidate)' accordingly. 2) 'Open AND short detection' is correct per RM0456 §64.1 and the ST moderator, but it means stuck-at/open on the loop (comparison of a PRNG pattern); a bypass short that wires TAMP_OUT directly to TAMP_IN around the mesh is indistinguishable from the mesh itself and the ST thread's follow-up on that case went unanswered. Only GridPlus-style impedance/waveform monitoring addresses that; the risks field should name it explicitly. 3) Trezor citation range: filter config is tamper.c:131-136, the passive TAMP_IN2 config is :157-160 (CR2 TAMP2TRG level-high) and :196-201 (CR1 TAMP2E); the PRODUCTION-only arm is in core/embed/projects/kernel/main.c:140-143 (secmon/main.c:113-114 disables it; prodtest/cmd/prodtest_tamper.c provides 'tamper-read'). 4) Keystone 3 Pro: the only primary evidence is the keystone3-firmware README ('PCI level anti-tamper protection'); it runs on MH1903 + ATECC608A/MAX32520/DS28C50, no mesh or certification is published. Downgrade to 'vendor-claimed intrusion erase' rather than a demonstrated mesh precedent. 5) Foundation Passport Prime: official glossary says tamper detection 'erases all sensitive data including your Master Key' — not a 'factory reset'; the display-tamper-pin statement comes from the 2025 audit-response PDF (seen only via a search snippet; the PDF and docs.foundation.xyz/glossary were fetched, the latter confirms the erase claim). 6) None of GridPlus/Keystone/Foundation uses the STM32U5 active-tamper block (GridPlus detection is in its 'SCE'); the precedent is for the mesh+erase concept, not the U585 implementation — there is no vendor precedent for U585 ATCR-driven meshes (Trezor on U5 uses passive only). 7) Repo context the proposal omits: docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:106-108 and :239 ALREADY specify a 4-layer mesh over U585 + both SEs into TAMP_INx plus a case switch (status 'board not started; firmware ext-pin cfg open'); the genuinely new parts are display-connector coverage, active mode/PRNG and PC13 assignment. 8) secure/src/hw_platform_under_test/pure_tests.rs:1728 negative_tamp_init_skips_external_pins asserts no TAMPxE bit is set and CR3=0 — enabling TAMP1E must update that gate. tamp.rs base address is already fixed (0x5600_7C00 at :127-132), but §10.1 of evt-silicon-validation.md:929 and issues #47/#75/#50/#248 (all OPEN) confirm no TAMP response has ever been silicon-validated. 9) RM0456 Table 650 confirms TAMP_IN/TAMP_OUT remain functional in VBAT mode, supporting the supercap-armed window claim.
